headline: Paused for your review. MVP revised on 8 Nov: AP and TN across every domain, government first plus labelled general research, and more intelligent reasoning. Completion so far (agriculture and finance): Andhra Pradesh 95% and 95%, Tamil Nadu 100% and 100%.
decisions: Your rules (6 Nov) stay in force: you are head of the project and I act as senior project manager; this page is updated only when you ask, with Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu completion in percent; data and engine are equal focuses; testing comes later.

Revised MVP (your words, 8 Nov): Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, every domain, not only agriculture and finance. Government documents stay the main and preferred source; general research from the web is added, always labelled as from the web. VETRA should reason and synthesise (for example the difference between agriculture in AP and TN, which no single document holds) instead of rejecting such questions, and a stronger model should write the final draft once the API budget allows. Plan, in order: deepen and broaden the data; review it by hand; tiered web search (official, then general); make it intelligent (routing, evidence grading, state profiles, outline-first answers); answer structure with a stronger writer. Researched, not built: see the Current plan tab.

Speed goal (your words, 9 Nov): the whole system with the least latency and replies as fast as possible. It applies to every MVP step: each change is measured for time as well as correctness. Today a general answer takes about 3 seconds, a standard one 20 to 60 seconds and a deep one 2 to 3.5 minutes. The ideas, to measure first (streaming the answer, fewer model calls, parallel searches, caching, a fast model for planning and a bigger one only to write, more than one question at a time, preparing profiles ahead), are on the Current plan tab. Not started.

Web search (MVP step 3), first version tried on 7 Nov, not satisfied, not tested: when VETRA's own data can't answer a part, it now searches official government websites live through Tavily (a web-search API: VETRA sends a search and an allowed-sites list, gets back page links, then reads the pages itself), and shows what it finds labelled 'Fetched live, not yet checked by VETRA', or says no official source was found. Nothing is stored. It was tried on a few questions only; no question set has been run and no answers read by hand. Details and known weaknesses are on the Current plan tab.

Answer structure (MVP step 4), foundation laid on 7 Nov, not tested: answers now follow question cases the way data follows aspects: comparison (a table), change, grievance, status, eligibility (yes, no or depends first), deadline (date and open or closed first), amount (figure and unit first), procedure (numbered steps), contact, options and explanation, each with a shape for quick, standard and deep answers. A code check stops answers saying something doesn't exist when the documents only don't mention it, and every answer's structure is now recorded. Tried on two live questions only. Details are on the Current plan tab.

General questions, first version (8 Nov), rigid on purpose: a question that needs no government record ("what is crop rotation") is now answered directly by the model in a few seconds, labelled as a general answer with no sources. Anything about a scheme, rule, money, rights or offices still goes through the records, and a general answer that states a rupee amount or percentage is sent to the records too. The line will be made more flexible later. Not tested on a question set.
Models (7 Nov, for now): Groq is primary and Gemini the fallback until you choose a paid API. The key is only in .env.

You are reviewing this page for the next few days. Nothing runs until you say to resume. The full technical account of how VETRA finds documents and checks answers is at the top of the Current plan tab.
next: Web search, first version (7 Nov): built in vetra/websearch.py and wired into the agent; state's own sites first (ap.gov.in, tn.gov.in), then other government sites; other states' pages skipped; passages must contain the subject's own words; same answer checks as held documents. Tried on two Andhra Pradesh questions: farm pond found district horticulture pages; silkworm shed found nothing official and the answer now says so instead of wrongly saying no subsidy exists. 247 code tests pass. Not tested on answers.

Answer structure foundation (7 Nov): vetra/structure.py holds 11 question cases with their answer shapes, the shared writing rules, the 'doesn't exist' check, a structure report on every answer and a repair for split tables. 19 of 19 sample questions sorted correctly (English, Telugu, Tamil). Live: a PMFBY versus RWBCIS comparison now opens with the answer and gives a table. 265 code tests pass.

General questions (8 Nov): the planner marks a question general; one direct call answers it with a label; a code guard sends answers with money figures back to the records. Live: crop rotation answered in 2.6 seconds; PM-KISAN amount still answered from the official record. 268 code tests pass.

Andhra Pradesh, deep level: agriculture 42 of 44 aspects have exact records (95%), 27 of 44 have three or more (61%); finance 20 of 21 (95%), 10 of 21 with three or more (48%). The aspects still without a record were searched and no official source exists: paddy bonus over MSP and a farmers' welfare board (agriculture), and a women's stamp duty concession (finance). Held: 217 documents, about 6,860 passages, 378 exact records.

Tamil Nadu, deep level: agriculture 44 of 44 aspects with exact records (100%), 36 of 44 with three or more (82%); finance 21 of 21 (100%), 13 of 21 with three or more (62%). Held: 190 documents, about 9,720 passages, 346 exact records.

Central rules that apply in every state: 72 records from 24 documents, including PM-KISAN, Kisan Credit Card interest and the new RBI KCC rules (from 1 Jan 2027), fertiliser prices, eNAM, land acquisition compensation, PMFME, drones, farm machinery subsidy (SMAM, Dec 2025), Soil Health Card and the Natural Farming Mission.

New on 7 Nov: Andhra Pradesh: freehold rights on assigned land (G.O.Ms.No.588), Amaravati land pooling, National Family Benefit Scheme, PMAY-Urban 2.0, mango price support, cooperative credit, finance commission grants, budget and debt, paraquat ban, fertiliser at RSKs, seed appeals. Tamil Nadu: women's 1% registration fee cut, construction and other workers' welfare boards, fishermen and traders boards, TAHDCO land purchase for SC/ST women, Annal Ambedkar scheme, soil fertility mission, sericulture, free farm power, tax arrears settlement, local cess.

Engine and code (243 tests pass): record lookups now search both topics, so a cooperative loan filed under agriculture answers a finance question; search drops repeated passages (two TN documents were held twice); the grounding check reads percentages and financial years and looks in central documents; a register (knowledge/searched.jsonl) records what was searched and not found, shown separately here; the build queue takes a lock so two builds never start together.
issues: Nothing is tested. Every count means held, not right. All 270 records whose source is held match their documents figure by figure; some were read from scans and are flagged. A person should review them before launch.

Web search is not finished: you are not satisfied with it yet and it hasn't been tested. Weak points: live pages can be old and undated, it adds 10 to 20 seconds, Tavily's free tier has a monthly limit, passage picking is plain word matching, and it can sometimes search when it didn't need to. Gemini, the fallback model, is also out of free quota, so answers rely on Groq.

Answer structure is only a foundation: not tested on a question set; case rules are instructions to the writer, and only the 'doesn't exist' rule is enforced by code so far; a deep comparison took about three and a half minutes.

Speed and queueing: the server answers one question at a time, so a deep answer (2 to 3 minutes on Groq's free tier) holds up the next question, and it keeps working even if the page is closed. General questions now skip this, but deep answers need to get faster.

Andhra Pradesh aspects with fewer than three records: agriculture: loan waiver, KCC, wildlife damage, seed, soil health, natural farming, drip, farm ponds, wells, solar pumps, dairy, food processing, tenancy, land conversion, land acquisition; finance: debt, finance commission, guideline values, state GST, land revenue, electricity duty, property tax, tax arrears, state loans, housing. Most need official AP orders that the GO index and reachable department sites don't have.

Tamil Nadu aspects with fewer than three records: agriculture: loan waiver, drip, sericulture, eNAM, food processing, land conversion, land acquisition, extension offices; finance: debt, finance commission, guideline values, land revenue, electricity duty, property tax, tax arrears, women concessions.

Percent caveat: completion counts keyword matches against each aspect, so the figures are a guide, not a grade; an aspect with one record counts as covered, which is why the three-or-more figure is shown beside it.
workers: Head of the project: decide, set priorities, ask for page updates
Plans, reads documents and enters exact records, designs and changes the engine and code, reports here when asked
Crawling, picking documents, downloads, OCR, order links, rate lines, search builds
Run only when started for a task
Reads scanned orders on the PC

log.text: Monitoring station set up on this page, with the architecture, diagrams and techniques updated. Today: first hand-marked test, 157 of 179 good, marked by me before the fixes. Added 36 exact rates across Andhra Pradesh deeds, vehicle tax and relief, Tamil Nadu vehicle tax and Chennai profession tax, all unreviewed. Engine: 3 checks added, 231 code tests pass. Listed 18,441 Andhra Pradesh orders and about 3,300 official PDFs. Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu aren't done.

You removed the fixed date, so work goes in logical order: collect, ask, read, fix, then the next state. Checked this page against the code and corrected it: tests are 231, exact records and scan reading are shown, and stale document lists are gone. The older Version 1 tabs are kept as history and weren't checked.
The aspect run stalled for about an hour because the free model limits ran out. It now uses gemini-3.1-flash-lite and stops itself after 3 misses in a row.

The test run is paused at 56 of 136 because it was too slow on free limits. 8 Andhra Pradesh records added from official orders: pensions, fishing ban relief and poultry. Next: more rates from documents already held, then the open data gaps.

8 more records from documents already held: Tamil Nadu pensions, fishing relief and electricity tax range; Andhra Pradesh rooftop solar for BC consumers and the closed property tax waiver. Test run stays paused. None of these has been through a full answer yet.

On your rule, no free models and no testing. 50 exact records entered tonight, including Tamil Nadu's official paddy incentive and crop loan waiver. PC is downloading picked orders with no model. New: each order's number and what it replaces is read automatically and carried through to the answer.

Morning report, 06:58. Since the 22:22 report: 49 exact records entered (42 agriculture, 6 finance, 1 date), 1 repeat removed. None has been through a full answer; all are marked unreviewed. Documents: 115 scanned Tamil Nadu agriculture orders fetched and read by OCR (27 routine ones dropped, 28 named from their abstracts), 1 Andhra Pradesh DEEPAM-2 order added. Builds: finance AP (+7 chunks), agriculture AP (no change), finance TN (no change), agriculture TN (+2,890 chunks from the scans). What failed: Tesseract crashed on one page at 01:40 and stopped the Tamil Nadu agriculture build; fixed so a bad page is skipped, test added, rebuilt by 02:56. My own failure: the hourly checks from 02:00 to 06:00 did not run, so the PC sat idle for about four hours after 02:57. Andhra Pradesh, added: horticulture subsidies (polyhouse, shade net, mulching, farm pond, nets, orchards, mushroom, pack house, machinery), paddy procurement KMS 2026-27, electricity duty range (from a Bill), free LPG cylinders and piped gas subsidy, pension eligibility, Annadatha, livestock insurance, Kharif 2026 drought, mango insurance date. Andhra Pradesh, still missing: electricity duty rate per category, guideline values, wildlife damage compensation, used-vehicle tax, women's stamp concession, ration entitlement, field-crop machinery subsidy. Tamil Nadu, added: state pension eligibility, Uzhavar Pathukappu, ration entitlement, unemployment aid, machinery hire 2026-27, solar fencing, threshing floors, drones for women, soil conservation, skimming wells, custom hiring centres, SC/ST borewells, ponds, dairy, native breeds, solar dryers. Tamil Nadu, still missing: women's 1% registration fee cut (press only), wildlife crop damage rates (G.O.(D) No.141 of 2016 not found online), Rabi 2026-27 insurance dates, notified electricity tax rate, KMS 2026-27 paddy incentive. Usage: 5-hour 5%, weekly 19% (last report's 20 and 14 were wrong; real then was 24 and 15). You asked me to keep going until 3 pm; I am.

Update on your request. New rules in force: you are head, I am senior project manager; page updated only when you ask, with completion percentages; no usage or pacing rules; data and engine are equal focuses; testing later. Completion at deep level (exact records): Andhra Pradesh agriculture 68%, finance 62%; Tamil Nadu agriculture 86%, finance 62%. Text held: AP 98% and 95%, TN 100% and 100%. Nothing tested. Background jobs stopped; waiting for your instruction.

Update on your request (7 Nov). Completion at deep level: Andhra Pradesh agriculture 95% of aspects with exact records (61% with three or more), finance 95% (48%); Tamil Nadu agriculture 100% (82%), finance 100% (62%). Aspects with no record in Andhra Pradesh were searched and have no official source; they are listed in a register. Other states are for the full product. The Current plan tab now opens with this plan and a step-by-step account of how VETRA plans, searches, checks and cites. Completion unchanged: Andhra Pradesh 95% and 95%, Tamil Nadu 100% and 100% of deep aspects with exact records. Paused for your review.

Update on your request (8 Nov). General questions: a first, deliberately rigid version of a direct path. If the planner judges that a question needs no government record, one model call answers it in a few seconds, labelled as general with no sources; scheme, rule, money and rights questions still go through the records, and a general answer with a rupee amount or percentage is sent to the records. Tried live: crop rotation in 2.6 seconds; PM-KISAN still cited from the record. Also noted: the server answers one question at a time, so slow deep answers hold up the next one. Completion unchanged.

Revised MVP goal on your request (8 Nov). Scope: Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu across every domain. Sources: government first and preferred, then official websites, then general websites, each labelled. Intelligence: route questions by what they need, grade evidence and widen the search, prepare state and domain profiles so comparisons like AP versus TN agriculture can be answered, write long answers outline-first, and use a stronger model for the final draft when the budget allows. Research gathered (Adaptive-RAG, Corrective RAG, Self-RAG, GraphRAG, RAPTOR, STORM, GPT Researcher, Open Deep Research, SAFE, and three books) and written on the Current plan tab. No code written.

Added to the MVP plan on your request (9 Nov): speed. The whole system should reply as fast as possible, and every step is now measured for time as well as correctness. Targets: general under 2 seconds, quick under 3, standard under 10, deep under 30 seconds to the first section. The causes found so far and what to try are on the Current plan tab. No code written.
